key_insight: SLIM learns to remove redundant material from 3D lattices while approximately preserving homogenized elasticity, replacing per-lattice topology optimization with a single neural prediction.
engineering_relevance: The model enables rapid refinement of existing lattice designs for lower material use without repeating costly constrained optimization.
method: Train a dual-octree implicit network on lattice pairs generated by property-constrained topology optimization.
Predict the signed-distance field of a lightweight lattice.
Penalize estimated stiffness changes using target-based homogenization sensitivities during training only.
evidence_signal: Across 906 held-out lattices, SLIM achieved 15.90% mean relative volume-fraction reduction, 90.51% lightweighting success, and 0.636% mean normalized aggregate TO-target error, with generation taking approximately 0.5 s versus 2516.0 s for direct topology optimization.
watch_item: Training requires optimized targets and sensitivity data; generalization beyond the evaluated lattice distribution remains unestablished.
paper_title: SLIM: Learning an Operator for Material-Efficient 3D Lattice Refinement
